relevance_audit.quote: On November 2, 2022, CoinDesk published a piece stating that a trading company called Alameda Research, also owned by Bankman-Fried, held a disproportionately large amount of FTX’s cryptocurrency token, or asset, called FTT. This triggered a competing cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, to sell all its shares of FTT. FTT’s value dropped significantly, and FTX began to search for new investments from venture capitalists. They also asked Binance for help. Their competitor agreed to buy FTX on November 8, 2022, but backed out of the deal on November 9. On November 11, Alameda Research and FTX declared bankruptcy, and Bankman-Fried stepped down as CEO of FTX.
